formation.title: The United Provinces
formation.text:
The seven provinces stand united at last. What began as a desperate revolt against tyranny has forged something the world has never seen, a republic of merchants and mariners, governed not by a crowned head but by the collective will of its States-General. The great question now is what kind of nation we shall become. Shall we turn our faces to the sea, as our shipwrights and admirals urge, building fleets to command every ocean and filling our warehouses with the riches of the Indies? Or shall we look inward to our unique gift, a society where the persecuted find refuge, where scholars debate freely, and where the printing press runs day and night? The world watches to see what this small, stubborn nation will make of its hard-won freedom.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

modifiers.name: Thalassocracy of the North
modifiers.text: The Dutch Republic commands the seas. From the herring busses of the North Sea to the great Indiamen of the VOC, our merchant fleets carry the wealth of the world to Amsterdam's quays. Where others see waves, we see highways.

options.text: Let all who seek freedom find it here.

modifiers.name: Cradle of Liberty
modifiers.text: The United Provinces stand as a beacon of tolerance in a divided Europe. Here, Catholics and Calvinists live side by side, Sephardic scholars print freely, and Huguenot refugees find shelter. Our universities and printing houses make Amsterdam the intellectual capital of the continent.

advances.name: Burgundian Cloth Trade
advances.text: The great cloth halls of Bruges, Ghent, and Ypres anchor a textile trade that stretches from English wool pastures to Italian luxury markets.

advances.name: Herring Fleets
advances.text: Dutch herring busses sail in great convoys to the fishing grounds, and new curing techniques preserve the catch for export across Europe.

advances.name: Civic Autonomy
advances.text: Netherlandish towns guard their chartered privileges fiercely, creating a tradition of burgher self-governance that no overlord can easily suppress.

advances.name: Waterschappen
advances.text: The water boards, democratic cooperatives older than any parliament, coordinate the endless labor of building dikes, draining marshes, and keeping the sea at bay.

advances.name: Watergeuzen
advances.text: The Sea Beggars harass enemy shipping from their raiding bases, striking fast and vanishing into the coastal shallows before heavier warships can respond.

advances.name: Leiden Textiles
advances.text: Flemish refugee weavers transform Leiden into Europe's greatest textile center, producing everything from fine lakens to light camlets and says.

advances.name: Union of Utrecht
advances.text: The founding treaty of the Republic guarantees freedom of conscience, an unprecedented commitment to religious tolerance that will draw persecuted minorities from across Europe.

event.title: The Union of Utrecht
event.text: In the great hall at Utrecht, representatives of the northern provinces have signed a treaty of perpetual union. Each province shall remain free in matters of religion, no person shall be persecuted on account of their faith. This unprecedented declaration of freedom of conscience binds the provinces together not through shared blood or a shared crown, but through a shared commitment to liberty. The Union of Utrecht shall serve as the foundation of our republic, a constitution born not of kings but of free citizens.

advances.name: Stadtholder Tradition
advances.text: The House of Orange-Nassau provides military leadership to the Republic, with stadtholders who combine princely authority with republican service.

advances.name: Schutterij Tradition
advances.text: Every Dutch town maintains its schutterij, civic militia companies of armed burghers who train regularly and defend their city walls with stubborn pride.

advances.name: VOC Charter
advances.text: The Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie, history's first publicly traded multinational corporation, holds sovereign powers to wage war and govern territories across Asia.

event.title: Charter of the VOC
event.text: The States-General has granted a charter to the Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie, the United East India Company. This is no mere trading firm. The VOC holds the sovereign right to wage war, negotiate treaties, and establish colonies in the name of the Republic. With a starting capital that dwarfs any enterprise in history, the Company will dispatch fleets of armed merchantmen to the Spice Islands, challenging the Portuguese monopoly over the eastern trade. Shareholders from every province have invested their fortunes in this venture, binding the Republic's destiny to the distant seas of Asia.

options.text: The spice trade shall be ours.

modifiers.name: Spirit of the VOC
modifiers.text: The chartered company opens the world to Dutch enterprise. Shareholders, sailors, and factors carry the orange flag to the farthest reaches of the globe.

advances.name: Fluyt Design
advances.text: The fluyt revolutionizes maritime commerce, a cheap, efficient cargo vessel requiring fewer crew than any rival design, giving Dutch shipping an unbeatable cost advantage.

advances.name: Admiralties
advances.text: The five admiralty boards of the Republic coordinate shipbuilding, naval operations, and convoy protection, projecting Dutch sea power from the Baltic to the East Indies.

advances.name: Freedom of Conscience
advances.text: The Republic's commitment to religious tolerance attracts persecuted minorities (Sephardic Jews, Huguenots, Mennonites) whose skills and capital enrich Dutch society.

advances.name: Wisselbank
advances.text: The Bank of Amsterdam introduces sound money and reliable credit, making guilder banco the trusted currency of international commerce.

event.title: The Wisselbank Opens
event.text: The city of Amsterdam has established its Exchange Bank, the Wisselbank, to bring order to the chaos of debased foreign currencies flooding our markets. Henceforth, all bills of exchange above six hundred guilders must be settled through the bank. Merchants deposit their coin and receive credit in bank money, guilder banco, whose value the city guarantees. No more clipping, no more debasement. The reliability of Dutch bank money will draw merchants from across Europe to settle their accounts in Amsterdam, making our city the clearing house of the world's trade.

options.text: Sound money is the foundation of commerce.

modifiers.name: Wisselbank Confidence
modifiers.text: The Bank of Amsterdam's guilder banco has become the most trusted currency in Europe. Bills drawn on the Wisselbank are accepted from Archangel to Cadiz.

advances.name: Amsterdam Beurs
advances.text: The world's first stock exchange enables the trading of company shares, commodity futures, and government bonds, the birth of modern finance.

advances.name: Korps Mariniers
advances.text: The Marine Corps of the Republic, established by Johan de Witt, provides elite amphibious infantry for combined naval-land operations.

advances.name: Dutch Ship of the Line
advances.text: The great warships of the Anglo-Dutch Wars carry rows of heavy cannons on multiple gun decks, designed for the devastating fleet engagements of open ocean warfare.

advances.name: Golden Age Mastery
advances.text: The Dutch Republic has achieved an unprecedented convergence of artistic brilliance, scientific discovery, and commercial supremacy, a golden age that illuminates all of Europe.

event.title: Masters of the Golden Age
event.text: The Dutch Republic has achieved a mastery of arts, sciences, and commerce that the world has rarely seen. Rembrandt paints in Amsterdam while Vermeer captures light in Delft. Huygens discovers Saturn's rings while Leeuwenhoek peers into his microscope at the invisible world teeming in a drop of water. The wealth of the Indies flows through our counting houses, and our merchant fleet exceeds that of all other nations combined. In this small country wrested from the sea, human ingenuity has reached new heights.

options.text: A golden age for the ages.

advances.name: Colonial Network
advances.text: From New Amsterdam to the Cape Colony, from Suriname to Batavia, Dutch colonial possessions form a global trading network knit together by the VOC and WIC.

advances.name: Batavian Reforms
advances.text: Revolutionary reforms modernize Dutch governance, replacing the old provincial federalism with centralized administration and rational bureaucracy.

advances.name: Hydraulic Engineering
advances.text: Dutch engineers have mastered the science of water, steam-powered pumping stations now drain entire lakes, creating new polders of fertile land from what was once open water.

advances.name: Mercantile Legacy
advances.text: Centuries of commercial enterprise have created a nation of traders, financiers, and entrepreneurs whose business networks span the globe.

destiny.name: Destiny of the Republic
destiny.text: The United Provinces have been proclaimed. Now we must decide: shall we command the oceans or illuminate the mind? Our stability must hold firm before we can begin.

event.title: The Republic's Destiny Awaits
event.text: The United Provinces stand at a crossroads. The foundations of our republic are firm, our stability assured. Now we must chart the course that will define our nation for generations. Two great visions compete for the soul of the Republic. One beckons us toward the open sea, toward distant ports and the wealth of the Indies. The other calls us to build something unprecedented in Europe: a republic of free inquiry, sound money, and enlightened governance.

options.text: Our destiny is in our hands.

destiny.name: Baltic Mastery
destiny.text: Control the great Hanseatic ports of Lubeck and Hamburg to dominate the northern trade routes that feed the Republic's wealth.

conditions.text: Own Lübeck, or a subject owns it
Own Hamburg, or a subject owns it

event.title: Masters of the Northern Seas
event.text: The orange flag now flies over the great Hanseatic ports. Lubeck, that ancient queen of the Baltic trade, has passed under our control. Hamburg, gateway to the North Sea and the German interior, answers to our admiralties. The grain ships from Poland, the timber fleets from Scandinavia, the herring convoys of the North Sea, all now pass through waters we command. Our dominance of northern commerce is complete, and our merchants turn their eyes toward even more distant horizons.

options.text: The Baltic is a Dutch lake.

destiny.name: The Spice Venture
destiny.text: Plant the Dutch flag over the Strait of Malacca and the clove-rich Moluccas, opening the eastern spice trade to our merchant fleets.

conditions.text: Own Malacca, or a subject owns it
Own Ternate, or a subject owns it

event.title: Foothold in the Spice Islands
event.text: Dutch merchants and soldiers have seized control of the legendary Spice Islands. Malacca, the great chokepoint of eastern trade, flies our colors, and the clove groves of Ternate are now ours to harvest. The question is how best to exploit this unprecedented opportunity. Shall we focus on building a commercial network of convoys and factors, squeezing every guilder from the spice trade? Or shall we invest in armed fleets that can sweep all rivals from these waters and establish permanent naval supremacy?

modifiers.name: Spice Convoy Network
modifiers.text: A vast network of armed merchant convoys carries the wealth of the Indies along protected sea lanes, with Dutch agents in every port gathering intelligence on rivals.

options.text: Build the war fleet of the Indies.

modifiers.name: Armed Fleet of the Indies
modifiers.text: A permanent war fleet patrols the eastern seas, sweeping rival navies from the spice routes while Dutch land forces grow neglected.

destiny.name: Global Thalassocracy
destiny.text: Build the complete maritime empire from Batavia to Ceylon, run from VOC Chambers and Company yards in three of our ports. The seas belong to the Republic, and our trading factories dot every shore.

conditions.text: Own Sunda Kelapa, or a subject owns it
Own Kotte, or a subject owns it
Has a VOC Chamber, Shipyard, Grand Shipyard or Naval Base in at least 3 locations

event.title: Empire of the Seas
event.text: From the counting houses of Amsterdam to the fortified factories of Batavia, from the cinnamon plantations of Ceylon to the pepper warehouses of the Spice Islands, the Dutch maritime empire now spans the globe. No nation has ever wielded such commercial power from so small a homeland. Our captains round the Cape as casually as fishermen row to the Dogger Bank. Now we must decide the character of this unprecedented empire. Shall we build permanent colonies and extract the wealth of the land? Or shall we rule the oceans themselves, making free trade the foundation of our hegemony?

modifiers.name: Batavian Dominion
modifiers.text: Dutch colonial settlements extract raw materials from across the tropics, driving population growth in the empire while stretching military manpower thin.

modifiers.name: Ocean Sovereign
modifiers.text: The Republic commands the world's sea lanes not through force alone but through free trade agreements and diplomatic prestige that make Dutch commerce welcome everywhere.

destiny.name: The Printing Revolution
destiny.text: Teach one in five of the realm's people to read and make the Netherlands Europe's publishing capital. Our presses shall print what others dare not speak.

event.title: The Presses of Amsterdam
event.text: The printing press has transformed the Netherlands into the publishing capital of Europe. What cannot be printed in Paris or London for fear of censorship rolls freely off our presses in Amsterdam, Leiden, and The Hague. French philosophes, English dissenters, German pietists, all find willing printers in our republic. Atlases, scientific treatises, theological debates, and seditious pamphlets pour from our workshops in every language of Europe. Knowledge has become our most profitable export.

options.text: Let the presses run day and night.

destiny.name: Financial Supremacy
destiny.text: Establish Amsterdam as the undisputed financial center of the world: raise its Beurs or a stock exchange, keep a thriving paper market, and build the town on the Amstel up into a great city.

conditions.text: Amsterdam is owned and has a Beurs or a Stock Exchange

children.text: Paper is produced in the market
Paper is traded in the market

conditions.text: We own Amsterdam and its development is at least 37

event.title: The Financial Capital of the World
event.text: Amsterdam, grown from a town on the Amstel into a great city, has become what no city has been before: the financial center of the entire world. Bills drawn on our banks are accepted from Archangel to Cadiz. Our commodity exchange sets prices that merchants in every port must follow. Government bonds, company shares, and futures contracts, financial instruments that exist nowhere else, flow through our counting houses daily. Now we must choose how to wield this unprecedented power. Shall we build a tolerant haven that attracts the best minds from every persecuted community? Or shall we forge a network of innovation that binds Europe's economies to our own?

options.text: Welcome all who bring talent and capital.

modifiers.name: Tolerant Haven
modifiers.text: Persecuted minorities (Sephardic Jews, Huguenots, Mennonites) flock to the Republic, enriching its merchant class even as the old crown prerogatives wane.

modifiers.name: Financial Hub
modifiers.text: Amsterdam's financial innovations (stock exchanges, futures markets, central banking) bind the economies of Europe together under Dutch leadership.

destiny.name: The Enlightened Republic
destiny.text: Teach two in five of the realm's people to read and bring Geneva's Calvinist intellectual tradition under our wing. Make Leiden, the seat of the Republic's first university, twice the town it was, and win scholarly renown.

conditions.text: Own Geneva, or a subject owns it
We own Leiden and its development is at least 38

event.title: The Enlightened Republic
event.text: The Republic has achieved what philosophers only dreamed of: a state governed by reason, enriched by tolerance, and illuminated by science. Leiden has doubled around its university, and our schools draw scholars from across Europe. Our observatories map the heavens, our microscopes reveal the invisible, our botanists catalogue the world's flora. With Geneva's intellectual tradition now under our protection, the Republic stands as the undisputed center of Enlightenment thought. How shall we shape this golden age of reason? As a republic of letters, where free thought transforms society? Or as a center of scientific mastery, where knowledge becomes power?

options.text: Let freedom of thought be our creed.

modifiers.name: Republic of Letters
modifiers.text: The Dutch Republic has become the intellectual heart of Europe, where free inquiry, liberal thought, and burgher literacy reach unprecedented heights.

modifiers.name: Golden Age of Science
modifiers.text: Dutch scientists lead the world in optics, cartography, and natural philosophy, creating a stable and prosperous society through the practical application of knowledge.

units.name: Watergeuzen
units.text: Fast raiding vessels crewed by the Sea Beggars, Protestant rebels who strike at enemy shipping from coastal havens.

units.name: Fluyt
units.text: The revolutionary Dutch cargo vessel, cheap to build, efficient to operate, and requiring fewer crew than any comparable ship.

units.name: Dutch Ship of the Line
units.text: A powerful warship bristling with heavy cannons on multiple decks, built for the fleet engagements of the Anglo-Dutch Wars.

units.name: Korps Marinier
units.text: Elite amphibious soldiers of the Dutch Marine Corps, trained for combined naval-land operations and ship-to-ship boarding.

units.name: Schutterij
units.text: Civic militia of armed burghers who defend their towns with the determination of free citizens protecting their own homes.

buildings.name: Beurs
buildings.text: A commodity and stock exchange where merchants trade shares, settle bills, and speculate on futures, the beating heart of Dutch commercial life.

buildings.name: Admiraliteit
buildings.text: An admiralty board that coordinates shipbuilding, repairs, and naval operations from its coastal headquarters.

buildings.name: Lakenhal
buildings.text: A great cloth hall where textiles are inspected, stamped with quality marks, and sold to merchants from across Europe.

buildings.name: Waterschap
buildings.text: A water board that coordinates dike maintenance, drainage, and flood prevention, keeping the sea at bay through collective action.

buildings.name: Haringpakkerij
buildings.text: A herring packing house on the quay, where the catch of the busses is gibbed, salted and sealed in barrels branded by the sworn packers of the Great Fishery.

where.text: The location's raw material is Fish

buildings.name: VOC Chamber
buildings.text: One of the home chambers of the East India Company, with its counting house, warehouses and wharf, where the return fleets are fitted out and their cargoes auctioned.

buildings.name: Diamantslijperij
buildings.text: A diamond cutting works, a trade brought north by the refugees of Antwerp and open to the Sephardim of Amsterdam because no guild governed it.

buildings.name: Factorij
buildings.text: A fortified Dutch trading factory where Company agents buy local goods, store spices for the return voyage, and fly the tricolor over foreign shores.

buildings.name: Universiteit
buildings.text: A great Dutch university where scholars pursue knowledge freely, attracting students from across Europe to study medicine, law, theology, and the natural sciences.

list.name: Staten-Generaal
list.text: The States-General assembles at the Binnenhof in The Hague, where one delegation per province deliberates the affairs of the Union. Major resolutions require unanimity, so the Raadpensionaris of Holland brokers endless compromises among the seven sovereign states. While the assembly endures, no edict carries weight without the regents' consent: an iron republican legitimacy bought at the price of glacial resolve.

list.name: Raad van State
list.text: Reorganised by the Instruction of 12 April 1588, the Council of State directs military finance, the war department, and the tax administration of the Generality Lands, and keeps the frontier fortresses on its yearly State of War. Stadhouders sit ex officio; ordinary members are nominated by the Provincial States. The Council is the Republic's permanent executive in matters of war and treasure, the office through which the noble service-class claims its share of the Republic against the Holland-burgher faction.

list.name: Heeren XVII
list.text: The Vereenigde Oost-Indische Compagnie chartered on 20 March 1602 vests sovereign powers (forts, treaties, war, and silver) in seventeen directors meeting alternately at Amsterdam and Middelburg. Eight come from the Amsterdam chamber, four from Zeeland, one each from Delft, Rotterdam, Hoorn and Enkhuizen, with the seventeenth seat rotating. The Heeren are merchants first and statesmen second, and our overseas empire bends to that order.

list.name: Wisselbank van Amsterdam
list.text: The Amsterdam Exchange Bank, founded by the city's vroedschap on 31 January 1609, sets the bank guilder as the unit of European wholesale finance. A municipal ordinance compels every bill of exchange over six hundred guilders payable in Amsterdam to clear through its books, and so every great merchant in Christendom keeps an account on the Dam. Where the Wisselbank's ledgers are sound, capital is cheap; where they slip, the whole edifice of Dutch credit shudders.

list.name: Vijf Admiraliteiten
list.text: The Five Admiralty Boards established by the States-General's Instruction of 13 August 1597 (de Maze at Rotterdam, Amsterdam, Zeeland at Middelburg, the Noorderkwartier at Hoorn and Enkhuizen, and Friesland at Dokkum) govern naval finance, dockyards, and convoying. About fifty councillors from all seven provinces serve, funded by the convooien en licenten customs duties levied at every Dutch port. This corporate-provincial fleet, not a royal navy, is what keeps our merchantmen afloat from Archangel to Batavia.

list.name: Waterschappen
list.text: The polderboards descend from the Hoogheemraadschap of Rijnland chartered in 1255. In every polder the heemraden assess each farmer's hoefslag, the section of dike bordering his land, and levy fines on neglected maintenance. The boards stand outside the provincial States and outlive every regime change (counts, Habsburgs, Republic, monarchy) because without them the sea returns. They are the deepest institution of the Low Countries, slow to dismantle and slow to restore.

list.name: Stadhouderschap
list.text: Originally the Habsburg sovereign's lieutenant in each province, the stadhouder survived the Revolt as a republican captain-general. The Princes of Orange hold most of the Republic's stadhouderates by quasi-dynastic right and command the Dutch States Army in the field. Their use of the schutterij militias to discipline rebellious cities makes them the perpetual rivals of the Holland regents: a monarchical reflex inside a federal republic.
